title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 87-89, section 1.3-1.4). Earlier pages set up a dictionary between several equivalent data on a base X/S:
- P^1-bundles with two disjoint sections;
- invertible sheaves Ω;
- rank-3 Lie algebra bundles 𝔤 of sl2-type with a split Cartan, 𝔤 ≅ Ω ⊕ O_X ⊕ Ω^{-1};
- PGL2/G-torsors with a 'couple de Killing'.

On this page Grothendieck parametrises connections on such a Lie algebra bundle 𝔤 (written 𝔍 in the transcription; it is the fraktur 𝔤 of the previous page).

Step 1. Choose a splitting 𝔤 ≅ Ω ⊕ Ω^0 ⊕ Ω^{-1} with Ω^0 = O_X. Put ω = Ω^1_{X/S}, so 𝔤⊗ω ≅ Ω⊗ω ⊕ ω ⊕ Ω^{-1}⊗ω.

Step 2. Locally choose a basis δ of Ω, giving a local frame (δ, 1, δ^{-1}) of 𝔤. In this frame the structure constants are constant, by the bracket table of p.87. So the trivial connection c_0(λδ+μ·1+νδ^{-1}) = δ dλ + 1 dμ + δ^{-1} dν is flat and respects the bracket.

Step 3. Any other bracket-compatible connection differs from c_0 by a section of Der(𝔤,𝔤)⊗ω. Since every derivation of an sl2-type algebra is inner (char ≠ 2), Der(𝔤,𝔤) ≅ 𝔤. So connections form a torsor under 𝔤⊗ω, with c_ϖ = c_0 + ad(ϖ) for ϖ = ϖ_2 ⊕ ϖ_1 ⊕ ϖ_0 in Γ(Ω⊗ω) ⊕ Γ(ω) ⊕ Γ(Ω^{-1}⊗ω).

The page ends just as he starts computing c_ϖ. The next page finishes the computation:
- With the filtration Fil (the Borel L = Ω ⊕ O ⊂ 𝔤), any connection satisfies Griffiths transversality c(Fil_i) ⊂ Fil_{i-1}⊗ω.
- The induced O-linear maps gr_i → gr_{i+1}⊗ω are c_{1,2} = -2ϖ_0 and c_{2,3} = ϖ_0. This relation, c_{1,2} = -2c_{2,3}, is independent of the splitting.
- Connections preserving the Borel (σ horizontal) are those with ϖ_0 = 0, a torsor under L⊗ω.
- The projection Conn → Ω^{-1}⊗ω, c ↦ ϖ_0(c), is canonical: a 'Kodaira-Spencer class'.

In modern terms this is the local structure theory of PGL2-connections on a bundle with a Borel reduction: the second fundamental form of an sl2-oper / indigenous bundle. When ϖ_0 is an isomorphism Ω ≅ ω (Kodaira-Spencer iso), one gets an oper. The purpose, given the cote (Gauss-Manin, Picard-Fuchs, Cartier), is presumably to analyse the Gauss-Manin connection on H^1_dR of a family of elliptic curves (or its symmetric square / ad bundle) together with its Hodge filtration. Presumably also its p-curvature via Cartier's operation.
errors: The written identification 'Hom(𝔤,𝔤)⊗ω ≃ 𝔤⊗ω' is literally false (Hom is rank 9). It must be read as Dér(𝔤,𝔤)⊗ω ≃ 𝔤⊗ω (derivations are inner), as the NB indicates. The image likely reads 'Dér'.
Innerness of derivations of sl2 needs 2 invertible. The previous page's margin raises char ≠ 2, but this page does not restate it.
c_0 respects the bracket only because the bracket table of p.87 gives constant structure constants in the frame (δ,1,δ^{-1}). This is implicit, not stated.
The computation of c_ϖ is left unfinished on this page ('≟ ... +'). It is completed on the next page, with sign conventions for the weights that are not checked here.

ideas.what: Connections on a Lie algebra bundle of sl2 type form a torsor under 𝔤⊗Ω^1, since all derivations are inner.
ideas.modern_name: Affine space of connections on a PGL2-torsor / adjoint bundle

ideas.what: Correspondence: P^1-bundle with two disjoint sections ↔ invertible sheaf Ω ↔ split sl2-Lie algebra bundle Ω⊕O⊕Ω^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of a PGL2-torsor to the torus G_m; adjoint bundle of a split torus reduction
ideas.where_published: Torsor/reduction formalism of SGA3 in general

ideas.what: Griffiths transversality of any connection relative to the Borel filtration, with second fundamental form Conn → Ω^{-1}⊗ω, and the relation c_{1,2} = -2c_{2,3} (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Second fundamental form / Kodaira-Spencer map of an sl2-oper (indigenous bundle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (indigenous bundles, 1967); Drinfeld-Sokolov (1985) and Beilinson-Drinfeld (opers); Katz (Kodaira-Spencer for elliptic curves)

missed.claim: In a Gauss-Manin/Picard-Fuchs/Cartier context (c. 1972), Grothendieck sets up the algebraic, characteristic-free (char ≠ 2) theory of PGL2-connections with Borel reduction over a general base X/S, and isolates the canonical Kodaira-Spencer-type invariant Conn → Ω^{-1}⊗ω. This is essentially the sl2-oper formalism later developed by Beilinson-Drinfeld. In char p, combined with the Cartier operator, it is the setting of Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (dormant opers). This is a precursor, not a result beyond the literature.
missed.quote: Une connexion générale s'obtient alors en ajoutant une section de Dér(𝔤,𝔤)⊗ω ≃ 𝔤⊗ω
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically documents that Grothendieck considered oper-like structures (indigenous bundles over arbitrary bases) linked to Cartier/p-curvature, predating Drinfeld-Sokolov and Mochizuki. Mathematically it is routine by today's standards.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page itself is routine: connections on a split sl2-bundle are c_0 + ad(ϖ). The interest is historical. Together with the next page it shows an early algebraic formulation of sl2-opers and their Kodaira-Spencer invariant in Grothendieck's Gauss-Manin/Cartier notes, which the literature does not credit to him.
transcription_corrections: The bundle written 𝔍 is the fraktur 𝔤 of the previous page (the Lie algebra bundle).
The NB likely reads '(NB toute dérivation de 𝔤 est intérieure)', not 'indécomposable'.
In the opening sentence, 'une splitting' is preceded by 'un'; the marginal 'i.e. un' is an insertion.
Under Ω^0 the vertical '||' with O_X indicates Ω^0 = O_X; the line 'Ω²' in the raw image is Ω^0.
